clue.text: Bloomer made by church congregations, say?

indicators.note: the question mark and 'say' ask for a word that is spoken like the phrase before it

parts.note: a parson's congregation is his flock, so several congregations are flocks

explanation.surface: A gaffe committed by assembled churchgoers, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder, but here it means something that blooms; the sound of FLOCKS gives the flower's spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is a flowering plant, and this garden perennial is grown for its bright clustered flowers.

clue.text: All-embracing fear gripping old farm animal

indicators.note: gripping means holding something inside

parts.note: panic is sudden fear
a ram is a male sheep kept on farms

explanation.surface: Terror seizes an ancient beast of the farmyard.
explanation.definitionFit: A panoramic view takes in the whole scene, embracing everything around.

clue.text: Restriction left one fellow bowled over

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: something bowled over is knocked over, turned upside down, so the word is read upwards

parts.note: Tim is a man's name, any fellow

explanation.surface: A cricketing curb: a single batsman left out after being bowled.
explanation.definitionFit: A limit is a boundary or restriction placed on something.

clue.text: Greek historian's element? Work hard in it

indicators.note: the work and hard pieces go in it, inside the element

parts.note: xenon is a chemical element, a noble gas
OP is short for opus, a work
H is short for hard on pencils

explanation.surface: A question about which chemical element an ancient writer belongs to, and a call to labour at it.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's means 'is': the historian is the element with work and hard put inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The Athenian soldier and writer who wrote the Anabasis was a classical Greek historian.

clue.text: Bond books featured in the Newcastle Journal?

indicators.note: a feature in a newspaper sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: NE is the postcode area for Newcastle upon Tyne
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible
a journal is a newspaper, a paper

explanation.surface: Spy novels are serialised in a regional newspaper from Tyneside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' suggests James Bond novels, but bond is a grade of good writing paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Bond is a heavy, high-quality writing paper, the kind used for letters.

clue.text: Beans, or bananas

definitions.meaning: ... and beans are both edible seeds
bananas is slang for crazy, mad

explanation.definitionFit: Both seeds like beans and craziness like bananas share this informal word.

clue.text: Shabby trio securing publicity ban

indicators.note: securing means holding inside

parts.note: a trio is three
an ad is an advertisement, publicity
to bar is to ban

explanation.surface: Three people impose a gag on advertising.
explanation.definitionFit: Threadbare clothes are worn thin and shabby from long use.

clue.text: Favourite way to wrap a firework

parts.note: a pet is a favourite
RD is short for road, a way

explanation.surface: A preferred method of covering a rocket.
explanation.definitionFit: A petard is an old explosive device, a firecracker or small bomb.

clue.text: National working in Asia kept English out

indicators.note: working signals the letters are put to work in a new order
out signals the English letter is left out of the rearranged pool

explanation.surface: A citizen employed in Asia kept the English away.
explanation.walkthrough: IN ASIA KEPT, minus E, is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A national of Pakistan, a citizen of that south Asian country.

clue.text: Roam mountains

definitions.meaning: to ... over an area is to roam it

explanation.definitionFit: To wander freely and a line of peaks both share this one word.

clue.text: One proposes to roam in northern resort

indicators.note: read as re-sort, sorting the letters again into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone plans to wander around a seaside town up north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday town but is the anagram signal, re-sort, applied to TO ROAM IN N.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who proposes a candidate for office or an award is said to nominate them.

clue.text: Nominal sanction welcomed by cardinal

indicators.note: being welcomed by something means being taken inside it

parts.note: ten is a cardinal number
to sanction is to approve, to OK

explanation.surface: A churchman of high rank approves some penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cardinal' suggests a churchman; here it is a cardinal number, TEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominal payment is a token one, small and symbolic rather than real.

clue.text: Produce amended description of military engineer?

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers of the British Army
a type is a kind or description, as in 'people of that description'

explanation.surface: Write a revised account of an army sapper.
explanation.definitionFit: To key a text in again, usually with corrections, is to produce an amended version.

clue.text: The French like this clue introduced for game

indicators.note: one piece is introduced into the other, placed inside it

parts.note: le is French for 'the'
the clue is an across clue in the grid

explanation.surface: A French phrase is brought into this puzzle clue for a sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like this clue' refers to the clue itself: it sits in the across list.
explanation.definitionFit: A field team sport played with netted sticks, originating with Native North Americans.

clue.text: Eat in a hurry, being held in check

parts.note: to sup is to eat supper
pressed for time means in a hurry

explanation.surface: Wolfing food down while rushed and restrained.
explanation.definitionFit: Something suppressed is kept down or restrained, held in check.

clue.text: Quiet lad's unfinished puzzle it's baffling

parts.note: keeping mum means keeping quiet

indicators.note: the word for lad loses its final letter

parts.note: a lad is a boy
the Times Jumbo is its giant weekend crossword puzzle

explanation.surface: A silent boy's half-done crossword is a mystery to him.
explanation.walkthrough: The Jumbo is the large-format crossword run by The Times.
explanation.definitionFit: Meaningless jargon or ritual, something designed to confuse and baffle the listener.

clue.text: Note with book identifies source of copper

parts.note: Malachi is a book of the Old Testament
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A remark in a volume points to where copper comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: Malachite is a green mineral and a copper ore.

clue.text: Spoils wetland, sending out horse

indicators.note: sending something out removes it from the word

parts.note: a marsh is waterlogged land
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: A rider ruins a bog by driving away his mount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horse' gives H through heroin slang, not any equine word.
explanation.definitionFit: To mar something is to spoil or damage it.

clue.text: Slightly knowing librarian within

indicators.note: the librarian is placed within, enclosed inside, the word for knowing

parts.note: sly means knowing, cunning
a librarian lends books, so is a lender

explanation.surface: A shrewd library worker is inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Slenderly means in a slight or meagre way, slightly.

clue.text: Popular ci-devant stoolie

parts.note: in means popular, fashionable
ci-devant is French for former, previous

explanation.surface: A one-time well-liked police informant.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoolie, short for stool pigeon, is one who informs to the police.

clue.text: Demand ring

definitions.meaning: a ... for something is a demand for it
to ring someone on the telephone is to phone them

explanation.definitionFit: Both a demand (a call for action) and a telephone ring share this one short word.

clue.text: Trainee a pair tempt to accept power

indicators.note: accepting something takes it inside

parts.note: to tempt is to entice
P is the symbol for power in physics

explanation.surface: A learner is lured by two people with promises of influence.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone learning a trade under a skilled master is a trainee.

clue.text: Egeus's daughter, a girl's girl

parts.note: her means belonging to a girl
Mia is a girl's name

explanation.surface: An Athenian father's daughter is one girl's friend.
explanation.walkthrough: In A Midsummer Night's Dream, Egeus is the father of Hermia.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream, Egeus is the father of this young woman.

clue.text: Crooked knight dismissed by East End press chief

indicators.note: the knight is dismissed, sent out of the word

parts.note: a Cockney is a native of the East End of London
N is the chess notation for a knight
ED, short for editor, heads a newspaper

explanation.surface: A dishonest knight is sacked by an East London newspaper boss.
explanation.walkthrough: East End here stands for COCKNEY, a Londoner from the East End.
explanation.definitionFit: Something askew or not straight is crooked, set at a slant.

clue.text: People such a pseud takes in

indicators.note: the phrase takes in the answer, holding it inside its letters

explanation.surface: Folk like that phony are fooled.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaps is an informal word for men, people in general.

clue.text: Stern fellow suffering from exhaustion

parts.note: the poop is the raised deck at a ship's stern
Ed is a man's name, any fellow

explanation.surface: A severe man is worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stern' looks like an adjective, but it is the back of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Being pooped is an informal way of saying worn out and tired.

clue.text: Genuine contract announced

indicators.note: announced means spoken aloud

parts.note: to pucker is to contract, wrinkle up

explanation.surface: A real agreement is declared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contract' looks like a noun but is a verb, to pucker.
explanation.definitionFit: Pukka, from Hindi, means genuine or authentic.

clue.text: Sweetheart's disappointing score

definitions.meaning: a term of endearment for a ... one

explanation.definitionFit: Both a loved one and a nil score in tennis share this word.

clue.text: Man on American chopper saw …

indicators.note: in an across answer one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: ax is the American spelling of axe
IOM is the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A fellow rides on a US helicopter and sees something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saw' looks like a verb or tool, but it is an old saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is a proverb or maxim, a self-evident truth.

clue.text: … Oxford manufacturer?

parts.note: an Oxford is a type of lace-up shoe, so its maker makes footwear rather than anything from the city

explanation.definitionFit: One who makes Oxfords, lace-up leather shoes, is a cobbler or footwear maker.

clue.text: Scarper, seeing King Edward on horseback

indicators.note: being on horseback means being in the saddle, so the pieces go inside

parts.note: one rides on horseback in the saddle
K is the chess abbreviation for king
Ed is short for Edward

explanation.surface: Running away when a monarch is spotted riding by.
explanation.definitionFit: To scarper is British slang for to run away quickly, to flee.

clue.text: Prepared to try a book that's unknown

parts.note: to try a book is to read it
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Willing to have a go at a novel of mysterious origin.
explanation.definitionFit: Being prepared means being all set, equipped and good to go.
